P07-002.rationale: The verse contrasts what the tongue of the wise does with what the mouths of fools do, a complete subject-for-subject antithesis with its own two verbs.
P07-002.rejected_alternative: Grouping this with Prov.15.1 as a speech-topic pair was considered and rejected; the lexical stock (tongue/wise/fools) does not recur between the two lines.
observed_substrate_signals: paired subjects lashon chakhamim / pi kesilim carry the whole contrast
verb pair teitiv / yabbia gives the antithesis its hinge
P07-002.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism; the wise-tongue/fool-mouth opposition recurs later in the chapter (15:7, 15:14) but not in an adjacent verse, so it stays outside this row's evidence.

P07-003.rationale: One flowing statement describes YHWH's eyes reaching any location, watching both evil and good; there is no adversative turn splitting it into two contrasted halves.
P07-003.rejected_alternative: Reading it as the opening line of a larger YHWH-themed unit with 15:4 was rejected: 15:4 has no divine-name token at all.
observed_substrate_signals: one flowing clause (bekhol maqom ... tsofot) rather than a two-part antithesis
the object pair ra'im/tovim closes the line without contrastive vav
P07-003.device_notes: Synthetic parallelism (one expanding statement, not antithesis); the first of nine exact-token YHWH verses in this chapter (sweep: 9 verses, exact skeleton token).

P07-005.rationale: A fool who spurns his father's discipline is set against one who attends to reproof and so shows prudence; the whole moral contrast is self-contained.
P07-005.rejected_alternative: A cluster with 15:32, which uses the same discipline/reproof vocabulary, was considered; the two are eleven verses apart, well outside any consecutive run.
observed_substrate_signals: subject pair evil / shomer tokhachat carries the antithesis
the discipline-reproof vocabulary of this verse recurs later in the chapter but not next door
P07-005.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism; belongs to the correction-vocabulary thread that runs through chapter 15, whose catchword-adjacency count sits at 7 of 32 pairs per the device inventory, too thin to chain this verse to its neighbors.

P07-007.rationale: The lips of the wise scatter knowledge, but the heart of fools does not do so; the contrast is completed within the line by the closing negation.
P07-007.rejected_alternative: Joining forward into 15:8, which opens the tocevat-YHWH pair, was tried and dropped: 15:7 has no divine-name token and no lexical overlap with 15:8.
observed_substrate_signals: subject pair sifte chakhamim / lev kesilim mirrors 15:2's wise/fool antithesis without repeating its wording
closing negation lo khen completes the contrast inside the verse
P07-007.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism, closed by a terse negated predicate rather than a second positive verb.

P07-008.rationale: Both lines open their second colon with a matching construct phrase תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Prov.15.8), repeated verbatim at the head of the next verse as תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Prov.15.9) — a two-verse, word-for-word repeat (sweep: 2 consecutive verses) — the sacrifice of the wicked and then the way of the wicked are each pinned to the same 'abomination to YHWH' formula, binding the pair into one boundary decision.
P07-008.rejected_alternative: Reading each verse as a separate single_proverb was the default starting point but was set aside once the repeated two-word phrase surfaced as a genuine consecutive catchword rather than a mere thematic echo.
observed_substrate_signals: exact construct phrase תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Prov.15.8) repeated verbatim at the head of the second colon in oshb:Prov.15.9 (sweep: 2 consecutive verses)
both lines share the resha'im/rasha wicked-root subject as well as the tocevat-YHWH predicate
P07-008.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism in both lines (sacrifice/prayer in 15:8, way/pursuer in 15:9); the repeated phrase is the cluster's driver, not the shared theme of divine displeasure by itself.

P07-011.rationale: The scoffer's dislike of being corrected and his refusal to approach the wise are two restatements of the same resistance, closing the verse as one thought.
P07-011.rejected_alternative: A pairing with 15:7 or 15:14 on the wise/fool axis was considered; both are non-adjacent to this verse, so no consecutive-run evidence supports it.
observed_substrate_signals: two negated clauses (lo ye'ehav / lo yelekh) restate one attitude rather than contrasting two
letz 'scoffer' does not recur elsewhere in this part

P07-012.rationale: A glad heart brightens the face, and sorrow of heart crushes the spirit; the inner state and its outward or further-inward effect are each given one clause.
P07-012.rejected_alternative: Extending back into 15:12 fails for lack of a shared root; extending forward into 15:14 was also tried and dropped on the same ground before the 15:14 heart-token turned out too generic to carry a cluster on its own.
observed_substrate_signals: lev appears in both cola of this verse as the constant subject of two different fates
face/spirit imagery (panim / ruach) is not repeated in the surrounding verses
P07-012.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism (gladness versus sorrow of heart).

P07-013.rationale: An understanding heart seeks knowledge while the mouths of fools feed on folly, a wise-heart/fool-mouth antithesis that closes the couplet on its own terms; the source carries a ketiv/qere pair immediately before the qere reading, an inline ketiv token דָּ֑עַת (oshb:Prov.15.14) preceding the qere ופני, which the inventory records as one note at this verse.
P07-013.rejected_alternative: Clustering this with 15:2, whose closing formula it echoes almost word for word, was rejected because the two verses sit twelve lines apart and no adjacent verse carries the same wording.
observed_substrate_signals: antithetic subject pair lev navon / pi kesilim
ketiv/qere note at Prov.15.14: an inline unpointed token precedes the qere reading (INLINE-KETIV HAZARD)
P07-013.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism; the closing line closely echoes 'the mouths of fools ... folly' at Prov.15.2, a non-adjacent repeat noted here as texture, not as cluster evidence.

P07-014.rationale: The afflicted person's days are named as hard, but a cheerful heart keeps a continual feast; affliction and cheer are opposed within one line.
P07-014.rejected_alternative: A cluster with 15:16-17 on the strength of the shared 'good/better' vocabulary was tried and dropped: this verse's tov is an adjective inside a clause, not the tov-min comparative construction that binds 15:16 to 15:17.
observed_substrate_signals: temporal totalizer kol yeme is answered by tov lev in the second colon
the comparative tov-min construction of the following pair is absent here
P07-014.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism (hardship versus continual feast); sits immediately before the tov-min pair without sharing its construction.

P07-030.rationale: The plans of the heart belong to a man, but the tongue's answer comes from YHWH; human deliberation and YHWH's shaping of the outcome are opposed within the verse.
P07-030.rejected_alternative: Treating 16:1 as the opening line of a nine-verse cluster running through 16:9 was considered and rejected: 16:8, inside that span, carries no divine-name token at all, breaking any gap-free run.
observed_substrate_signals: le-adam ma'arche lev is answered by u-me-YHWH ma'aneh lashon
lev and adam recur at 16:9 as a non-adjacent bracket, disclosed as texture below
P07-030.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism; forms a non-adjacent inclusio with 16:9 (both pair lev with adam and both name YHWH as the one who determines the outcome) that is noted as cross-seam texture rather than treated as cluster evidence, since 16:2-16:8 lie between them and do not uniformly share the construction.

P07-031.rationale: A man's ways can look clean to him in his own eyes, but YHWH weighs the spirits; self-assessment and divine assessment are set against each other.
P07-031.rejected_alternative: Grouping this with 16:1 under one YHWH-sovereignty heading was rejected: beyond the divine name itself, the two verses share no repeated token.
observed_substrate_signals: kol darkhe ish zakh be-einav is answered by ve-tokhen ruchot YHWH
no lexical overlap with 16:1 beyond the divine name
P07-031.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism (self-perceived purity versus YHWH's inward weighing).

P07-032.rationale: An imperative to commit one's deeds to YHWH is followed by a promise that the plans will be established; command and consequence, not contrast, fill the verse.
P07-032.rejected_alternative: A join with 16:2 on the shared divine name was tried and dropped for the same reason noted there: no other token is shared, and this verse is a command while 16:2 is a statement.
observed_substrate_signals: imperative gol opens the verse rather than a descriptive noun clause
machshevoteikha echoes machshavot at 15:22 non-adjacently

P07-033.rationale: YHWH has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for the day of trouble; the verse states one sweeping claim about divine purpose rather than opposing two subjects.
P07-033.rejected_alternative: A join with 16:3 on the shared divine name and imperative mood was rejected: 16:4 is declarative, not an imperative-plus-result structure, and shares no other token with 16:3.
observed_substrate_signals: kol pa'al YHWH la-ma'anehu opens the verse as a totalizing claim
the concessive gam rasha extends rather than opposes the opening claim

P07-034.rationale: A proud heart of any kind is an abomination to YHWH, and such a one will surely not go unpunished; the verse intensifies its own claim in the second clause rather than opposing a second subject.
P07-034.rejected_alternative: Reading this as part of a gap-free YHWH-token run from 15:33 through 16:9 was rejected once 16:8, which falls inside that span, was confirmed to carry no divine-name form at all.
observed_substrate_signals: tocevat YHWH construct phrase recurs here from 15:8-9 and 15:26 non-adjacently
yad le-yad lo yinnakeh intensifies rather than contrasts the opening claim
P07-034.device_notes: Synthetic (intensifying) parallelism; the recurring tocevat-YHWH formula is disclosed as texture linking this verse to 15:8-9/15:26 without being adjacent to any of them.

P07-035.rationale: By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of YHWH one turns from evil; two synonymous means-clauses build one point about the sources of moral change.
P07-035.rejected_alternative: A join with 16:5 on the shared divine name was tried and dropped: no other token repeats, and 16:5 states a consequence while 16:6 states a means.
observed_substrate_signals: chesed ve-emet and yirat YHWH stand as parallel instrumental phrases
yirat YHWH echoes 15:33's yirat YHWH non-adjacently, seven lines earlier

P07-036.rationale: When a man's ways please YHWH, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him; the verse states one conditional outcome rather than opposing two subjects.
P07-036.rejected_alternative: A join with 16:6 was tried on the strength of the shared divine name; the two verses otherwise share no token, so the row was kept as its own single_proverb.
observed_substrate_signals: birtsot YHWH darkhe ish opens a conditional clause completed by the enemies-at-peace result
darkhe ish echoes 16:2's kol darkhe ish non-adjacently

P07-037.rationale: A little with righteousness is better than great income with injustice; the comparative shape is complete in one line and carries no divine-name token at all.
P07-037.rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into a wider YHWH-cluster spanning 15:33-16:9 was rejected on a direct textual ground: within that span, 16:8 alone has no form of the divine name, breaking the run at this exact point.
observed_substrate_signals: tov me'at opens the same comparative formula used at 15:16, but the two verses are not adjacent
no form of the divine name, prefixed or bare, appears anywhere in this verse
P07-037.device_notes: Synthetic comparative parallelism (tov-min construction); this verse is the reason a YHWH-token cluster cannot run gap-free from 15:33 through 16:9 — the run stops here and resumes at 16:9.

P07-038.rationale: A man's heart plans his course, but YHWH directs his steps; planning and outcome are opposed within the verse, echoing 16:1's opening contrast without being adjacent to it.
P07-038.rejected_alternative: Extending a cluster back through 16:8 to reach 16:1 was rejected because 16:8 (the immediately preceding verse) shares no divine-name token or other lexical link with 16:9.
observed_substrate_signals: lev adam yechashev darko is answered by va-YHWH yakhin tsa'ado
lev and adam both recur from 16:1, a non-adjacent inclusio noted at that row as texture
P07-038.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism; together with 16:1 forms the non-adjacent lev/adam/YHWH inclusio noted there, disclosed here again for symmetry but not used to merge the two rows since 16:2-16:8 intervene without uniform support.

P07-039.rationale: Both verses carry mishpat: בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט (oshb:Prov.16.10, 'in judgment') and מִ֭שְׁפָּט (oshb:Prov.16.11, 'a balance and scales of judgment') — a royal oracle that does not err in judgment is immediately followed by honest weights that belong to YHWH, two sayings on the standard of right judgment held together by the shared noun. Both verses also carry a paseq seg per the inventory (single-witness at each), a corroborating tier-3 signal rather than the boundary driver.
P07-039.rejected_alternative: Extending this pair forward to include 16:12-16:15 (the melekh/melakhim run) was considered but not adopted here: 16:11 itself carries no melekh token, so folding it into that run would claim continuity the bytes do not sustain; it is treated as its own mishpat-linked pair instead.
observed_substrate_signals: mishpat shared by oshb:Prov.16.10 and oshb:Prov.16.11 (sweep: 2 consecutive verses)
paseq recorded at both Prov.16.10 and Prov.16.11 in the inventory (single-witness)
P07-039.device_notes: Both lines are synthetic rather than antithetic; the pair sits immediately before the melekh/melakhim run of 16:12-16:15 without sharing that run's specific catchword.

P07-040.rationale: Each of these 4 verses carries the royal noun: מְ֭לָכִים (oshb:Prov.16.12, plural 'kings'), מְ֭לָכִים (oshb:Prov.16.13, plural 'kings'), מֶ֥לֶךְ (oshb:Prov.16.14, singular 'king'), and מֶ֥לֶךְ (oshb:Prov.16.15, singular 'king') — a gap-free four-verse run naming kings (sweep: 4 of 4 verses), moving from kingship's abstract standard (wrongdoing as abomination, righteous lips as delight) to its concrete effect on a courtier's life (the king's wrath, the king's favor).
P07-040.rejected_alternative: A wider six-verse 'kings run' proposed for 16:10-16:15 was tested and cut back: 16:11 carries zero instances of the melekh/melakhim root, so it is drafted with 16:10 as its own mishpat-linked pair instead, and this row is bounded to the 4-verse span where the royal noun recurs verse by verse.
observed_substrate_signals: melekh/melakhim token present in every verse of oshb:Prov.16.12 through oshb:Prov.16.15 (sweep: 4 consecutive verses)
the root shifts from plural (melakhim, 16:12-13, third-person observation about kings generally) to singular (melekh, 16:14-15, a courtier's experience of one king)
P07-040.device_notes: 16:12 and 16:14 read as synthetic/antithetic hybrids (an abomination clause explained by a ki-clause; wrath opposed by a wise man's pacifying), while 16:13 and 16:15 are synonymous; this is the strategy's named 'kings run' candidate realized at the span the bytes actually sustain.

P07-044.rationale: One who heeds the word finds good, and whoever trusts in YHWH is blessed; the verse pairs two synonymous conditions of well-being rather than opposing them.
P07-044.rejected_alternative: A join back to 16:19 on the shared tov root was tried and dropped: 16:19 uses tov as the opening comparative of an antithetic verse, while 16:20 uses it as the object of its opening clause, with no other shared token.
observed_substrate_signals: maskil al davar and u-voteach ba-YHWH give two parallel conditions
no royal-domain or pride vocabulary carries over from 16:18-19

P07-048.rationale: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones; one image is unpacked across two effects rather than opposed to a second subject.
P07-048.rejected_alternative: A join with 16:23 on the shared 'lips/speech' domain was tried and dropped: no specific token repeats between the two verses beyond the general topic of speech.
observed_substrate_signals: tsuf devash imre no'am opens the figurative predicate answered by two effect-clauses
marpe la-atsem echoes 15:30's tedashen atsem non-adjacently
P07-048.device_notes: Synthetic (synonymous) parallelism, unpacking one image across two effects.

P07-051.rationale: Three consecutive verses open with the identical word ish followed immediately by a construct-genitive vice-noun: אִ֣ישׁ בְּ֭לִיַּעַל (oshb:Prov.16.27, 'a worthless man'), אִ֣ישׁ תַּ֭הְפֻּכוֹת (oshb:Prov.16.28, 'a perverse man'), and אִ֣ישׁ חָ֭מָס (oshb:Prov.16.29, 'a violent man') — the identical opening word and matching grammatical template across three straight verses is a consecutive construction run, broken cleanly at 16:30, which opens with a participle instead of ish. The x-small nun (other_segs, single-witness) sits inside this span at Prov.16.28, a scribal seg disclosed here as texture, not as boundary evidence. Prov.16.27 also carries a ketiv/qere note on the word for 'lips', disclosed for completeness though it plays no role in the ish-opening evidence that drives this row.
P07-051.rejected_alternative: Reading each of the three as its own single_proverb was the default starting point and was set aside once the identical opening word and matching genitive-construct template were confirmed across all three verses in a row, with the run confirmed to stop cleanly at 16:26 before it and 16:30 after it.
observed_substrate_signals: ish opens oshb:Prov.16.27, oshb:Prov.16.28, and oshb:Prov.16.29 in immediate succession (sweep: 3 consecutive verses), each followed by a construct-genitive vice-noun
16:30 breaks the run by opening with a participle (otseh) rather than ish
x-small nun (other_segs, single-witness) at Prov.16.28
P07-051.device_notes: All three lines are synonymous (synthetic) parallelism, describing a type of troublemaker through a subject-plus-verb-plus-object clause; this three-verse run, sharing one opening word across three consecutive lines, is offered as directly-evidenced construction-run cohesion in this part.

P07-055.rationale: The lot is cast into the lap, but its outcome belongs to YHWH; human action and divine determination are opposed within the verse, closing the chapter on the same note it opened on at 16:1.
P07-055.rejected_alternative: A join back to 16:32 was tried and dropped: no shared token links the self-mastery saying to this closing verse about the lot and YHWH.
observed_substrate_signals: ba-cheiq yutal et ha-goral is answered by u-me-YHWH kol mishpato
mishpato echoes the mishpat token of 16:10-11 non-adjacently, twenty-three lines earlier
P07-055.device_notes: Antithetic parallelism; closes the chapter with the same human-act/YHWH-determines pattern that opened it at 16:1, a non-adjacent inclusio disclosed here as texture, not as a boundary driver.
